primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Antecedent for elliptic-side Tricomi boundary regularity. The independent proof supplies the full self-adjoint boundary energy calculation, lower-term absorption, rough regularization, complete microlocal iteration and model sharpness.

source_correspondence: H0 retains the original scalar real quadratic principal symbol, noncharacteristic face, complex lower coefficients, intrinsic solution and forcing, and actual Dirichlet trace. On the gliding set outside the closure of the hyperbolic set, a uniform negative normal derivative and nonpositive boundary tangential symbol give the complete elliptic-side inequality on a fixed collar.

W1 proves the weighted half-line inequality with no zero-trace assumption, using a compact piecewise-linear cutoff, exact dilation and the zero-norm cases. Fourier transformation and Holder give the full mixed-index estimate. W2 proves the actual trace estimate and a two-jet extension, retaining both arbitrary boundary values and the full normal derivative interpolation.

E0 uses the complete adjoint calculus to put the real principal symbol into a self-adjoint tangential operator. Its exact complex-valued energy identity contains both the normal-value pairing and the negative derivative-of-operator boundary form. All original complex lower terms remain in explicitly bounded operators.

E1 applies the uniform sharp lower bound with its order-one remainder. Weighted interpolation gives two thirds of a tangential derivative on the normal derivative, and the actual normal trace has order one third. The boundary value therefore has the sufficient five-thirds index. Every absorption coefficient is chosen after the relevant controlling inequality.

E2 proves the weighted second-order estimate using the full Lambda A Lambda inverse conjugate. Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz retains the normal weight. The second weighted inequality yields four-thirds tangential control. Lower tangential and normal norms are absorbed using the two independently proved interpolation facts.

E3 absorbs all complex lower terms and proves every real tangential Sobolev order through full conjugation, including its complete remainders. The value-trace exponent is a sufficient bound; optimality of that exponent is not asserted.

R0 uses uniformly order-zero compact convolution regularization. The complete commutator has tangential order one plus order minus one on the normal derivative. The original two-normal-derivative starting domain, explicit two-jet normal smoothing and actual trace convergence justify use of the smooth estimate. Bounded-norm limits identify all four gained terms.

R1 extends the real principal symbol by a convex combination, preserving all local lower coefficients. The exact fixed-collar data theorem and pure-normal guard make separated-symbol errors smooth with all normal jets. Errors of the normal cutoff occur in a strictly elliptic interior region and are controlled there before the degenerate estimate is used.

R2 supplies the actual finite starting order through noncharacteristic normal recovery, retaining restriction norms and original traces. Its displayed localized equation contains the forcing, complete commutator, normal-cutoff term and comparison/proper-kernel remainder. The order-one error leaves a one-third gain. Finitely many intermediate cones give every requested order on the same fixed final cone and collar; the differentiated equation recovers every normal derivative.

R3 proves both implications of the boundary-wavefront equality, using the original actual value trace. The result applies to intrinsic distributions and does not impose an energy-solution hypothesis or replace the boundary realization.

Three complete solutions verify every fractional index, a nonzero boundary energy contribution of size four, and sharpness of the four-thirds interior gain using compact zero-trace packets at normal scale lambda to the minus two thirds. The smooth figure profile has closed support endpoints [1,2]; its nonzero region and logarithmic first axis are stated precisely.

Forty exact checks verify the complex Green identity, interpolation indices, both extension jets, boundary example and layer scales. All 249 formulas and 25 displays parse; all mobile display and figure extents are accessible.
